claims.text: Adding a minor amount of boron to a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy before quenching will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding a minor amount of boron will improve the thermal stability of the resulting amorphous structure relative to the undoped base alloy.
The undoped phosphorus-containing alloy is difficult to vitrify or forms an unstable amorphous state.
The proposed boron addition is a few atomic percent.
Uniformly distributed boron atoms will disrupt short- and medium-range atomic order.
Disruption of short- and medium-range order by boron will increase atomic packing frustration.
Increased atomic packing frustration will impede crystal nucleation.
Increased atomic packing frustration will impede crystal growth.
Boron will interfere with the atomic rearrangements required for crystallization.
Boron will promote chemical heterogeneity in the alloy.
Boron will increase configurational entropy in the alloy.
Disruption of atomic clustering will enhance glass-forming ability.
The boron-doped alloy will have a lower critical cooling rate or a higher probability of amorphous-phase formation than the undoped alloy.
The boron-doped alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than the undoped alloy.
The predicted improvement requires boron to be uniformly incorporated into the alloy.
The predicted comparison requires doped and undoped samples to be processed using the same melt-processing and quenching conditions.
